strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Turning an ad hoc credit model into a formal pricing function spanning self-serve credits, enterprise contracts and model-level pricing.
strategy_updates.current_model: Per its pricing page: Free (125 one-time credits), Standard $15/mo or $12/mo annual (625 credits), Pro $35/mo or $28/mo annual (2,250 credits), Max $95/mo or $76/mo annual (9,500 credits, one month of rollover), Enterprise on request; Standard/Pro credits do not roll over; top-ups from 1,000 credits never expire; Gen-4.5 costs 12 credits per second; enterprise promotion of two months free usage for contracts signed by 10/31.
posting_evidence: Pricing Lead, remote US (NYC/SF preferred), USD 290K–360K; in Product, tied to the self-serve business.
Owns self-serve plan structure, credits, top-ups, billing cadence and regional pricing with ongoing experiments.
Designs the self-serve-to-enterprise path (contract structures, sales guardrails) and sets launch and lifecycle pricing for Runway models plus margins on third-party models.
Build mandate: publish pricing principles and value metrics, run a pricing council with Product, Finance, Research and GTM, and hire a small team.
Asks for 10+ years with 5+ owning pricing decisions, cost-to-serve and margin modelling from compute and inference inputs.
strategy_updates.interpretation: Runway appears to be moving pricing from product-by-product decisions to a governed function, as inference costs and a mix of first- and third-party models make margin per credit harder to manage. Inference: hosting third-party models alongside its own means credit prices have to reflect very different cost-to-serve, which explains the emphasis on compute-based margin models. The enterprise promotion on the pricing page and the self-serve-to-enterprise mandate suggest the company is pushing upmarket. The hire would be the first dedicated pricing owner, with wide scope and little existing infrastructure.
open_questions: Will credits stay the single value metric across Runway and third-party models, or move to model-specific pricing?
How much enterprise revenue exists today, and who owns enterprise discounting before this hire?
What budget and headcount come with the 'small pricing team'?
strategy_updates.caveat: No dated pricing news was read today; the analysis rests on the posting copies and the live pricing page, and the Ashby page itself did not render its body.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Managing AI feature margins through credit-based allowances layered onto raised subscription prices.

posting_evidence: Senior Lead, AI Pricing & Margin Strategy, New York, hybrid 2–3 days; USD 125,800–170,200; Greenhouse first published 2026-09-22.

Tracks model-provider pricing (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) and competitor AI packaging.

news.summary: A pricing tracker recorded Squarespace raising US monthly prices for Basic ($16 to $19), Core ($23 to $29) and Plus ($39 to $49) while Advanced stayed at $99, and renaming the 'Squarespace AI' plan label to 'Built-in AI Tools'.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Squarespace raised base prices this summer and now meters AI through plan-level credits, so the open problem is keeping AI costs inside those allowances as usage grows. The posting's focus on token-to-credit conversion, model routing and overage rules suggests credit allowances and overages are still being designed or tuned (inference). Watching third-party model prices fits a business whose AI cost base depends on outside providers. This is an analytical, margin-protection role rather than ownership of headline price levels.
open_questions: Will Squarespace sell AI credit top-ups or overages, which the pricing page does not list today?
Who sets headline plan prices: the Commercial Lead, Finance or Product?
How did the July price increase affect churn on Basic and Core?
strategy_updates.caveat: The price-increase item comes from a third-party tracker, not a Squarespace announcement; the pricing page was read in Canadian dollars.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Shifting ChatGPT and Codex from flat subscriptions toward token-based credits and usage limits shared across agentic features.
strategy_updates.current_model: Per OpenAI's Codex pricing docs: Free $0, Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro from $100/mo ($100/$200/$500 tiers), Business $20/user/mo annual ($25 monthly), Enterprise/Edu by contract; included usage limits per five-hour window vary by model; extra usage bought as credits on a token-based rate card (credits per 1M input/cached/output tokens by model); Codex and ChatGPT Work share one allowance and credit pool; GPT-5.6 Sol promotional pricing runs through at least 2026-11-21.
posting_evidence: Pricing Strategist, San Francisco, hybrid; Built In lists 234K–260K; posted about 3 days before 2026-10-23.
Reports to the Head of Product Pricing for Chat & Codex, a separate pricing team from the API role already tracked.
Mandate: plan usage limits, credits and overages, and new monetization models, backed by usage analysis, financial models and pricing experiments.
Sets up lightweight pricing governance (decision frameworks, approvals, performance tracking) with Product, GTM and Finance.
Asks for 6+ years in strategy and 3+ years hands-on pricing, including launching self-serve subscription or usage-based offers.
strategy_updates.interpretation: OpenAI has already moved Codex to a token-based credit rate card and merged agentic features into one shared allowance, so the subscription plans now work as bundles of compute rather than flat access. This role likely sets where included limits end and paid credits begin across tiers, which is the main lever for margin as heavier agentic usage grows (inference). Separate pricing heads for API and for Chat & Codex suggest consumer/business plans and the developer platform are priced on different logics that still need to stay consistent.
open_questions: How are included limits set per tier relative to compute cost, and how often will they change?
Will Business and Enterprise seats move fully to credit-based billing?
How does this team coordinate with API pricing on shared models and rates?
strategy_updates.caveat: OpenAI's own job page and help-center rate card could not be read; the posting details come from Built In, and no dated pricing announcement from the last three months was read today.

The posting's focus on partner profitability and bundled offerings fits that. For an analyst, it means building the models behind partner deals during an ownership change.
